- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is bullish (positive sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged bullish sentiment runs — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or median.
- When sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0.2), model tends to overcorrect downward — increase forecast slightly to avoid deep sell-off bias.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delays) are overpredicted — apply a 1–2 day lag correction in forecast smoothing.
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), reduce forecast volatility — use moving average or median smoothing to avoid overreaction.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, mean reversion is stronger than model suggests — apply a 10–15% downward bias if recent 10-day average is above 70.
- Overshoots after spikes are common — cap forecast at 10% above recent 5-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.7), forecast should align with recent 14-day moving average — avoid drifting too far from it.
